statement: Arts 5–6 enumerate the five nonsingular real species with line counts 27,15,7,3,3. The preceding existence statement realizes all cases.

source.version: Original Philosophical Transactions 153(1863),193–241; JSTOR original-journal scan

scope: Nonsingular real cubic surfaces in real projective three-space; count real projective lines, not only lines with a specified affine incidence.
notes:
The two 3-line species are distinguished by additional geometry. Equal real counts do not identify chambers.

The 1863 paper explicitly states that its nonsingular-cubic theory reproduces and develops Schläfli’s 1858 article. The earlier attribution is included; the 1863 text remains the inspected classification source.
